input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged
input.rationale: I searched the whole Agreement for any audit, inspection, verification, records-examination or usage-monitoring right binding Client and found none. § 5 (Compensation) and § 6 (Documentation and Disputes) run only in our favour — TrueLink must supply supporting documentation on request and Client may contest charges (p0047); there is no reciprocal right for TrueLink to audit Client's books, usage or records. § 8 (Client covenants) imposes compliance, access-restriction and content warranties but no audit or inspection right (p0050–p0058). The only access-related provisions favour Client (real-time usage statistics and log files via the Interface, p0037) or concern TrueLink's own Y2K remediation work (p0060), not verification of Client. With no Vendor audit right at all, Client has no exposure on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, so the position is better than both the preferred and fallback checklists and there is nothing to redline; the absence benefits us and should not be flagged. If TrueLink later proposes an audit right, we would hold it to the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where possible, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to Client systems).
